notes:
Mercedes-Benz MFA compact cars: W176 A-Class (2012 to 2018), W246 B-Class (2011 to 2018), C117 CLA (2013 to 2019) and X156 GLA (2014 to 2020).

The bus is the OBD socket's 11-bit CAN at 500 kbit/s (stated for a W246 by w246-b180cdi-obd; OBDb's captures also use 11-bit identifiers). Units speak UDS: a W176 capture in Memostats-V2 shows `10 03` answered with `50 03 00 14 00 C8`, identification read through `22 F1 00`, `22 F1 11`, `22 F1 21` and `22 F1 8C`, and fault codes through `19 02 0D`, so the profile opens the extended session 0x03 as the official app's scan does. The engine also answers service 22 in the default session (w246-b180cdi-obd, OBDb).

Most units reply on 0x4xx identifiers, not on the request plus 8, and a clone adapter that only passes replies on 0x7E8 to 0x7EF (reported by w246-b180cdi-obd) will hear the engine and the 0x7Ex units only.

The address table is transcribed from Memostats-V2's W176 catalogue, which its author took from the MBito app's database: 70 request and response pairs, 23 of them on one W176's record and reported answering a scan there, with raw frames captured for three (SCCM166, TPM_172, PARK117). The rest are catalogue entries, which may be optional equipment or other markets' units. One 0x7E2 unit comes only from OBDb. The units carry W246, C117 and other chassis numbers in their names (EPS246, HVAC246, PARK117, FCW246), which is the basis for applying the table to the whole platform; for the W246, C117 and X156 that reach is an inference, apart from the engine, transmission and 0x7E2 and 0x7E5 units that OBDb and w246-b180cdi-obd show on those cars. OBDb is cited for addresses only (CC-BY-SA-4.0); no signal definitions are copied.

Treat every row as unconfirmed on a given car until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering. Sources and their limits are in docs/vehicles/mercedes-compact.md.
